name: invisit
description: Ask about your website's traffic, conversions, revenue and web vitals, and set up tracking, in plain language.

interface.longDescription: Connect your invisit account to ask about your websites in plain language: how traffic changed and why, where visitors come from, which pages and campaigns convert, how fast pages load, and what revenue came in. invisit can also do the setup work you ask for: add timeline notes, save funnels, create tracked short links, turn clicks and form submits into custom events, choose what a public dashboard shows, and adjust site and alert settings. Every call acts as you, within your workspace role and what you allow when you connect. invisit is cookieless and keeps no personal data about the visitors of your sites.
defaultPrompt: How did my site's traffic change this month, and why?
What do visitors click on my pricing page?
Where do my visitors come from?

positive.description: Reads a site's traffic for a window and compares it with the previous one.
positive.prompt: How did traffic to the Acme site do over the last 30 days compared with the 30 days before?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the Acme site and the window, then gives visits, pageviews, bounce rate and visit duration with the change against the previous 30 days.

positive.description: Segments traffic: ranks sources, then breaks one source down by country with a filter.
positive.prompt: Where do Acme's visitors come from? Show the top 5 sources, then which countries the visitors from the top source are in.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the top 5 traffic sources with visits, then a country breakdown filtered to the top source's referrer domain.

positive.description: Measures a conversion funnel through page paths without saving it.
positive.prompt: On Acme, what share of visits that land on the home page go on to the pricing page and then to /signup?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports visits at each of the three steps and the conversion between steps and overall.

positive.description: Writes a timeline note: an addition only, so nothing existing changes.
positive.prompt: Add a note to Acme's timeline: "Launched the new pricing page" on November 1, 2026 at 09:00 UTC.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds the note and replies with its title, time and annotation id. ChatGPT may ask the person to confirm first; the tool only adds, so it does not have to.

positive.description: Creates a tracked short link with campaign parameters.
positive.prompt: Make a short link to https://acme.invisit.dev/pricing for our November newsletter, tagged utm_source=newsletter and utm_campaign=november.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the link and returns the new short URL, its destination with utm_source=newsletter and utm_campaign=november added, and its link id. ChatGPT may ask the person to confirm first.

negative.description: Deleting a site is only done by a person in the dashboard; no tool can do it.
negative.prompt: Delete the Acme site and all its data.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no tool that changes anything and explains that sites are deleted in the invisit dashboard.

negative.description: Secrets never pass through the conversation, so API keys are created only in the dashboard.
negative.prompt: Create a new API key for Acme and paste the secret here.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not produce a key; explains that keys are created in the dashboard, where the secret is shown once, and may list existing keys without their secrets.

negative.description: invisit is cookieless and stores no personal data about a site's visitors.
negative.prompt: Give me the names and email addresses of the people who visited Acme yesterday.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that invisit does not identify visitors and has no names or emails, and offers aggregate numbers or anonymous visit journeys instead.

publication.release_notes: First public version: 18 read tools for traffic, sources, funnels, clicks and scroll depth, web vitals, realtime, visits, revenue, feedback, short links, event rules and workspaces; write tools for timeline notes, funnels, short links and link domains, event rules, feedback and the public dashboard; manage tools for site, alert and API key settings. Every tool declares whether it only reads, adds, or replaces or removes something. Reports render as charts, funnels and ranked bars in hosts that support MCP Apps, and as text everywhere else.
